name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+22 partisan lean in a heavily Republican district
Incumbent advantage with no polling to suggest a race
model.rationale: The district's R+22 lean, Griffith's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing his win at about 96% all point the same direction, with no polls or headlines indicating a competitive race. Powers' minimal fundraising gives no evidence to move off the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any unexpected polling showing Griffith under 60% or a surge of outside spending against him would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Virginia's 9th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in Virginia, with a partisan lean of R+22. Morgan Griffith, the incumbent since 2011, is running for another term after easily securing renomination. Joy Powers, the Democratic nominee, has raised only about $85,000 with roughly $14,000 on hand, while Griffith has raised nearly $1.8 million and holds almost $1 million in cash. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

No public general-election polling is available, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 2% chance. The forecast expects Griffith to win by roughly 19 points, consistent with the district's fundamentals, and classifies the race as Safe Republican.
